title: 开始阅读最后更新：2026-07-27 06:28:17 最新章节：第130章侠义照肝胆
content_zh:
暮春的长安，本该是柳丝抽絮、莺鸣燕舞的时节，朱雀大街两侧的酒旗在暖风中缓缓舒展，往来行人衣袂轻扬，连空气里都浸着新酿米酒的清甜与牡丹的浓香。可位于皇城之侧的靖安侯府，却半点没有这人间烟火的暖意，青砖铺就的庭院里，几株老槐虽枝繁叶茂，却挡不住廊下那抹挺拔身影周身的清冷。
萧琰负手立于廊前，指尖无意识地摩挲着腰间悬着的“寒锋”剑鞘。那剑是他弱冠之年，西凉都护卫凛所赠，剑鞘由沙枣木所制，经多年摩挲已泛出温润的包浆，鞘身刻着细密的西疆纹样，末端缀着一枚小小的铜铃，平日里静置时不响，唯有策马疾驰时，才会发出清越短促的声响，像是西疆的风在低语。他身着一袭月白锦袍，未束玉带，长发仅用一根素木簪束起，眉眼深邃如寒潭，鼻梁高挺，唇线偏薄，明明生得一副俊朗无俦的模样，周身却萦绕着一股生人勿近的疏离。
谁都知道，这位靖安侯府的世子，三年前自西凉归来，便褪去了一身戎装，终日闭门不出，或读书练字，或抚剑沉思，再未涉足朝堂半步。三年前，他随护凛将军驻守西凉，大小战事亲历数十场，凭一己之力破了匈奴铁骑的“合围阵”，凭一柄寒锋剑斩杀匈奴三员大将，年少成名，意气风发，本该是朝堂之上最耀眼的新星，却在一场大胜之后，突然请辞归乡，褪去甲胄，甘为长安一闲客。
府中下人皆不敢多问，唯有萧琰自己清楚，那场大胜的背后，是多少西凉将士的鲜血与白骨，是护凛将军为护他周全，身中三箭，险些魂归西疆。他归来，是为了替那些战死的将士守着这长安的安稳，也是为了养精蓄锐，待他日西凉有需，便再披甲胄，奔赴边疆。只是这三年，长安太过安稳，安稳到让他有时会恍惚，仿佛那些金戈铁马、血染沙场的日子，只是一场遥远的梦。
“世子，天凉了，该回屋了。”老管家福伯端着一碗温热的茶，轻手轻脚地走上前来，语气里满是小心翼翼。福伯看着萧琰长大，见证过他少年意气、策马扬鞭的模样，也见过他归来时满身伤痕、沉默寡言的状态，心中满是疼惜，却又不敢多言半句。
萧琰微微颔首，目光却依旧望向西方，仿佛透过层层楼宇，能看到那千里之外的西凉大地。“福伯，西疆近来可有消息？”他的声音低沉，带着一丝不易察觉的期盼，这三年来，他每日都会问及此事，哪怕得到的总是“一切安好”的答复，也从未间断。
福伯叹了口气，将茶碗递到他手中，轻声道：“回世子，前几日收到驿站传来的消息，说西凉边境安稳，匈奴未有异动，护凛将军一切安好，还托人捎来了一些西疆的葡萄干，奴婢已经收起来了。”
萧琰接过茶碗，指尖传来一丝暖意，却暖不透心底的寒凉。他轻轻抿了一口，茶水清甜，却压不住他心中的忧思。他了解护凛，也了解西凉，那片土地常年风沙弥漫，匈奴铁骑虎视眈眈，从来都没有真正的安稳。所谓的“一切安好”，或许只是驿站传来的慰藉之词，或许，是护凛不想让他担心，刻意隐瞒了什么。
“知道了。”萧琰淡淡应道，将茶碗递还给福伯，转身走进了书房。书房内陈设简洁，案几上摆着笔墨纸砚，一侧的书架上，摆满了兵书战策，还有一些关于西凉地理、人文的典籍，皆是他这三年来反复研读之物。案几上，还放着一张泛黄的地图，那是西凉边境的地形图，上面用红笔标注着密密麻麻的关隘、要塞，还有一些他亲自标注的战场旧址，每一处，都承载着一段刻骨铭心的记忆。
他走到案几前，缓缓展开地图，指尖落在“雁门关”三个字上。那是西凉边境最重要的关隘，也是他当年与护凛将军并肩作战、浴血坚守的地方。还记得那年冬天，匈奴铁骑大举来犯，雁门关被围三日三夜，粮草断绝，水源枯竭，将士们煮雪为饮，拆木为薪，却没有一个人退缩。他与护凛将军并肩站在城楼上，寒风吹裂了他们的脸颊，鲜血染红了他们的甲胄，却依旧目光坚定，死守关隘，最终等到了援军，击退了匈奴铁骑。
想起那些日子，萧琰的眼底泛起一丝泪光，那些与他并肩作战的将士，那些鲜活的面容，仿佛就在眼前，他们笑着、喊着，挥舞着手中的兵器，为了守护西凉大地，为了守护身后的家国，不惜抛头颅、洒热血。可如今，他却身处长安的温室之中，过着安稳自在的日子，而那些将士，却依旧在西疆的风沙中坚守，随时都可能面临生死考验。
就在萧琰沉浸在回忆之中时，书房外突然传来一阵急促的脚步声，伴随着下人慌乱的呼喊：“世子！世子！大事不好了！驿站传来急报，西凉战事吃紧，雁门关危在旦夕！”
那声音急促而慌乱，打破了书房内的宁静，也像一把重锤，狠狠砸在萧琰的心上。他猛地站起身，身形一晃，手中的寒锋剑险些出鞘，眼底的疏离与平静瞬间被惊涛骇浪所取代，声音带着一丝不易察觉的颤抖：“慌什么！把急报拿进来！”
片刻之后，一名浑身是汗、衣衫凌乱的驿卒跌跌撞撞地跑了进来，手中紧紧攥着一封染血的书信，书信外用火漆封口，火漆已经被磨得模糊不清，显然是经过了千里加急，一路疾驰而来。驿卒双膝一软，跪倒在地，大口大口地喘着粗气，声音嘶哑地说道：“世……世子，急报……西凉急报，护凛将军……护凛将军派人送来的，说……说匈奴大举来犯，调集了十万铁骑，围攻雁门关，如今雁门关已被围五日五夜，粮草断绝，水源枯竭，将士们伤亡惨重，护凛将军……护凛将军身中数箭，危在旦夕，恳请世子……恳请世子速带援军，驰援西凉！”
萧琰几步走上前，一把夺过那封染血的书信，指尖因为用力而微微发白，连呼吸都变得急促起来。他颤抖着双手，撕开书信的封口，信纸已经被汗水和血迹浸湿，上面的字迹潦草而凌乱，还带着一些暗红色的血痕，显然是护凛将军在重伤之下，亲自写下的。
“萧琰吾弟：匈奴大举来犯，十万铁骑压境，雁门关危矣。今我军粮草断绝，水源枯竭，将士伤亡过半，我身中数箭，恐难支撑。西凉之地，乃家国屏障，不可有失；雁门关之险，乃西疆门户，不可不守。吾弟素有雄才大略，勇冠三军，今西凉告急，百姓危矣，将士危矣，恳请吾弟速归，聚旧部，提劲旅，驰援雁门关，护我西凉百姓，守我家国疆土。切记，西凉不可失，雁门关不可破，纵使拼尽最后一滴血，也要守住这西疆大地……护凛绝笔。”
短短百余字，萧琰却看了一遍又一遍，每一个字，都像一把尖刀，狠狠扎进他的心底，每一道血痕，都在诉说着西凉的危急与艰难。护凛将军，那个待他如兄、教他用兵、护他周全的人，如今身中数箭，危在旦夕；那些与他并肩作战的将士，如今身陷重围，伤亡惨重；那片他曾经用生命守护的土地，如今正遭受着匈奴铁骑的践踏，百姓流离失所，生灵涂炭。
“噗——”一口鲜血从萧琰的嘴角溢出，染红了手中的信纸，也染红了他的月白锦袍。他只觉得胸口一阵剧痛，仿佛有万千根针在扎着他的心脏，眼前阵阵发黑，却依旧死死攥着那封染血的书信，不肯松手。三年的隐忍与安稳，三年的等待与期盼，在这一刻，全部化为泡影，取而代之的，是无尽的悲痛与焦急，是刻入骨髓的责任与担当。
“世子！世子您怎么样？”福伯听到动静，急忙跑了进来，看到萧琰嘴角的鲜血，还有他手中染血的书信，吓得脸色惨白，连忙上前想要扶住他。
萧琰摆了摆手，推开福伯的手，强撑着身体，缓缓站直，眼底的悲痛渐渐被坚定所取代，那是一种破釜沉舟、视死如归的坚定，一种舍我其谁、义无反顾的决绝。他抬手擦去嘴角的鲜血，声音低沉而有力，带着不容置疑的威严：“福伯，备甲！备马！取我寒锋剑来！”

“世子！您三思啊！”福伯连忙劝阻，泪水在眼眶里打转，“您三年前身受重伤，如今身体尚未完全痊愈，而且您已经褪去甲胄，归乡闲居，朝堂之上，未必会同意您驰援西凉啊！再说，匈奴十万铁骑，来势汹汹，雁门关已被围多日，如今驰援，无异于虎口拔牙，九死一生啊！”
“三思？”萧琰冷笑一声，目光望向西方，眼底满是怒火与坚毅，“福伯，你可知，护凛将军待我如兄，那些西凉将士，皆是我的手足，那片西凉大地，是我曾经用生命守护的土地！如今，他们身陷重围，命悬一线，百姓流离失所，遭受涂炭，我岂能坐视不管？岂能三思而后行？”
他顿了顿，声音愈发沉重：“三年前，我之所以归乡，是为了替那些战死的将士守着这长安的安稳，是为了养精蓄锐，待他日西凉有需，便再披甲胄，奔赴边疆。如今，西凉有难，雁门关告急，正是我该回去的时候了！纵使前路九死一生，纵使朝堂不予支持，纵使孤身一人，我也绝不会退缩！我萧琰，生于乱世，死于沙场，本就是宿命，能为守护家国、守护手足而死，死而无憾！”
福伯看着萧琰坚定的目光，听着他决绝的话语，知道自己再劝也无用，只能含泪点了点头：“老奴……老奴这就去备甲、备马！”说完，便转身匆匆跑了出去。
萧琰再次走到案几前，目光落在那张西凉地形图上，指尖缓缓划过那些关隘、要塞，脑海中飞速思索着驰援之策。匈奴十万铁骑，来势汹汹，而雁门关如今粮草断绝，将士伤亡过半，护凛将军重伤，局势已然岌岌可危。他如今身在长安，手中无兵无卒，想要驰援西凉，绝非易事。
他想起，三年前他归乡之时，有一批西凉旧部，因为思念故土，也因为感念他的恩情，随他一同回到了长安，如今皆隐居在长安城外的村落之中，这些人，皆是身经百战、勇猛善战之士，若是能将他们召集起来，便是一支不小的力量。除此之外，他还可以派人联络西凉边境的其他守军，让他们派兵增援，两面夹击，或许能解雁门关之围。
还有，朝堂之上，虽然他已归乡闲居，但靖安侯府世代忠良，深受皇室信任，他或许可以入宫面圣，恳请陛下派兵增援西凉，调拨粮草、军械，支援雁门关。只是，他也清楚，如今的朝堂，奸臣当道，陛下沉迷享乐，早已没有了当年的雄心壮志，想要让陛下派兵增援，绝非易事，甚至可能会遭到奸臣的阻挠与排挤。
但即便如此，他也绝不会放弃。为了护凛将军，为了那些西凉将士，为了西凉的百姓，为了守护家国的疆土，他愿意不惜一切代价，哪怕是得罪奸臣，哪怕是触怒龙颜，哪怕是孤身一人，也要奔赴西凉，驰援雁门关。
片刻之后，福伯便带着几名下人，抬着一副亮银色的甲胄走了进来，那甲胄是萧琰当年在西凉时所穿，甲身由寒铁打造，上面刻着细密的纹路，既能防御刀剑，又轻便灵活，甲胄的胸前，还刻着一个大大的“萧”字，历经沙场磨砺，依旧熠熠生辉。寒锋剑也被取了来，剑身出鞘，寒光凛冽，映得整个书房都一片清冷，那是饱饮过匈奴鲜血的剑，是守护西凉大地的剑。
萧琰褪去身上的月白锦袍，在仆人的搀扶下，缓缓穿上那副甲胄。甲胄依旧合身，只是穿上的那一刻，他仿佛又回到了三年前的西凉战场，回到了那些金戈铁马、血染沙场的日子，身上的疲惫与疏离，瞬间被一身的戎装与锐气所取代，周身萦绕着一股舍我其谁的威严与决绝。他接过寒锋剑，握在手中，剑身的寒意透过指尖传来，却让他更加清醒，更加坚定了奔赴西凉的决心。
“福伯，”萧琰转过身，目光望向福伯，语气沉重地说道，“我今日奔赴西凉，驰援雁门关，此去凶险，不知能否平安归来。府中之事，就托付给你了，你一定要好好照料府中的下人，守护好靖安侯府的基业。还有，替我照顾好那些西凉旧部的家人，若是我此次未能归来，便告诉他们，莫要悲伤，莫要忘记西凉的百姓，莫要忘记守护家国的责任。”
福伯跪倒在地，泪水终于忍不住流了下来，哽咽着说道：“世子放心，老奴定不辱使命，好好照料府中之事，守护好靖安侯府的基业，照顾好旧部的家人。老奴恳请世子，一定要保重身体，平安归来，老奴和府中的下人，还有那些旧部，都在长安等您回来！”
萧琰微微颔首，眼中泛起一丝泪光，却强忍着没有掉下来。他知道，此去西凉，九死一生，或许，他再也回不来了，再也见不到福伯，再也见不到那些西凉旧部，再也见不到这长安的繁华与安稳。但他别无选择，他是萧琰，是靖安侯府的世子，是西凉的守护者，守护家国，守护手足，守护百姓，是他与生俱来的责任，哪怕付出生命的代价，也在所不辞。
“起来吧。”萧琰轻声说道，伸手扶起福伯，“时间紧迫，我不能再耽搁了，即刻出发，召集旧部，赶赴西凉。”
说完，他便提着寒锋剑，转身走出了书房，大步流星地穿过庭院，走向府门。庭院里的老槐树叶，在风中轻轻摇曳，仿佛在为他送行，又仿佛在为他担忧。阳光透过树叶的缝隙，洒在他的甲胄上，折射出耀眼的光芒，照亮了他坚定的身影，也照亮了他奔赴西凉、视死如归的决心。
府门外，一匹通体乌黑、神骏非凡的骏马早已备好，那是他当年在西凉时的坐骑，名为“踏雪”，能日行千里，夜行八百，当年陪着他南征北战，立下了赫赫战功。踏雪看到萧琰，发出一声悠长的嘶鸣，仿佛在诉说着思念，又仿佛在整装待发，随时准备跟随他奔赴战场。
content_en:
Late spring in Chang'an is supposed to be the time when willows are fluttering and warblers are singing and swallows are dancing. The wine flags on both sides of Zhuque Street are slowly unfurling in the warm wind. The clothes of passers-by are fluttering lightly. Even the air is soaked with the sweetness of newly brewed rice wine and the fragrance of peonies. But the Jingan Marquis Mansion, which is located on the side of the imperial city, does not have the warmth of this worldly fireworks at all. In the courtyard paved with green bricks, although a few old locust trees have luxuriant branches and leaves, they cannot block the coolness of the tall figure in the corridor.
Xiao Yan stood in front of the corridor with his hands behind his back, his fingertips unconsciously rubbing the "Han Feng" sword sheath hanging on his waist. The sword was given to him by Lin, the guard of the Xiliang capital, when he was in his weak years. The scabbard was made of Elaeagnus jujuba wood, and had become moist and patinated after years of rubbing. The scabbard was engraved with fine patterns of the Western Border, and there was a small copper bell at the end. It usually made no sound when it was left alone. Only when the horse was galloping, it would make a clear and short sound, like the whisper of the wind in the Western Border. He was dressed in a moon-white brocade robe, without a jade belt, and his long hair was only tied up with a plain wooden hairpin. His eyebrows were as deep as a cold pool, his nose was high, and his lip line was thin. He was obviously handsome and handsome, but there was a sense of alienation around him that kept strangers away from him.
Everyone knows that the eldest son of the Marquis of Jing'an Mansion, when he returned from Xiliang three years ago, took off his military uniform and stayed behind closed doors all day long, either reading and practicing calligraphy, or stroking his sword and meditating, and never set foot in the court again. Three years ago, he was stationed in Xiliang with General Hu Lin, and witnessed dozens of battles. He single-handedly broke through the "encirclement formation" of the Huns' cavalry, and killed three generals of the Huns with a cold-edge sword. He became famous at a young age and was high-spirited. He should have been the most dazzling star in the court, but after a great victory, he suddenly resigned and returned home, took off his armor, and became a wanderer in Chang'an.
No one in the mansion dared to ask more questions, but Xiao Yan himself knew clearly how much blood and bones of Xiliang soldiers were behind that great victory. It was General Hu Lin who was shot by three arrows in order to protect him, and he almost returned to the Western Frontier. He came back to protect the stability of Chang'an for the soldiers who died in the battle, and to recharge his batteries. When Xiliang needed it in the future, he would put on his armor and go to the frontier. It's just that in the past three years, Chang'an has been too stable, so stable that he sometimes feels in a trance, as if those days of fighting and blood-stained battlefields were just a distant dream.
"Your Majesty, it's getting cold, it's time to go back to the house." The old butler, Uncle Fu, walked forward gently with a bowl of warm tea, his tone full of caution. Uncle Fu watched Xiao Yan grow up, witnessed his youthful spirit, riding a horse and whipping his whip, and also saw his scarred and taciturn state when he returned. His heart was filled with pity, but he did not dare to say a word.
Xiao Yan nodded slightly, but still looked to the west, as if through the layers of buildings, he could see the land of Xiliang thousands of miles away. "Uncle Fu, is there any news from Western Xinjiang recently?" His voice was low, with a hint of unnoticeable expectation. In the past three years, he had asked about this every day, and he had never stopped even though he always received the answer of "everything is fine."
Uncle Fu sighed, handed the teacup into his hand, and said softly: "Hui Shizi, I received news from the inn a few days ago, saying that the Xiliang border is stable, the Huns have not moved, and that General Hu Lin is fine. I also asked someone to bring some raisins from Western Xinjiang, and my servant has put them away."
Xiao Yan took the tea bowl, feeling a hint of warmth at his fingertips, but it couldn't warm the coldness in his heart. He took a sip gently. The tea was sweet, but it couldn't suppress the worry in his heart. He knew Hu Lin, and he also knew Xiliang. That land was filled with wind and sand all year round, and the Xiongnu cavalry were eyeing it. There was never any real stability. The so-called "everything is fine" may be just words of comfort from the inn, or maybe Hu Lin doesn't want him to worry and deliberately hides something.
"I know." Xiao Yan responded calmly, handed the tea bowl back to Uncle Fu, turned around and walked into the study. The furnishings in the study room are simple. There are pens, inks, paper and inkstones on the desk. The bookshelf on one side is filled with military books and strategies, as well asSome classics on Xiliang's geography and humanities were things he had studied repeatedly over the past three years. There is also a yellowed map on the desk. It is a topographic map of the Xiliang border. It is marked with dense passes and fortresses in red pen, as well as some old battlefield sites that he personally marked. Each place carries an unforgettable memory.
He walked to the desk, slowly unfolded the map, and his fingertips landed on the three words "Yanmen Pass". That was the most important pass on the Xiliang border, and it was also the place where he fought side by side with General Hu Lin and defended it with blood. I still remember that winter, the Huns' cavalry invaded in large numbers. Yanmen Pass was besieged for three days and three nights. Food and grass were cut off, and water sources dried up. The soldiers boiled snow for drink and demolished wood for fuel, but no one flinched. He and General Hu Lin stood side by side on the city tower. The cold wind cracked their cheeks and the blood stained their armor. However, they still had a firm gaze and guarded the pass. Finally, they waited for reinforcements and repelled the Huns' cavalry.
Thinking of those days, there was a trace of tears in Xiao Yan's eyes. The vivid faces of the soldiers who fought alongside him seemed to be right in front of him. They laughed, shouted, and waved the weapons in their hands. In order to protect the land of Xiliang and the country behind them, they did not hesitate to throw their heads and blood. But now, he is in the greenhouse of Chang'an, living a stable and comfortable life, while those soldiers are still holding on in the wind and sand of Western Xinjiang, and may face life and death tests at any time.
Just when Xiao Yan was immersed in memories, there was suddenly a burst of hurried footsteps outside the study, accompanied by the panicked shouts of the servants: "Your Majesty! Your Majesty! Something bad has happened! An urgent report came from the inn. The war in Xiliang is serious, and Yanmen Pass is in danger!"
The voice was urgent and panicked, breaking the tranquility in the study, and hitting Xiao Yan's heart like a heavy hammer. He stood up suddenly, his body swayed, and the cold sword in his hand almost came out of its sheath. The alienation and calmness in his eyes were instantly replaced by the turbulent waves, and his voice had an imperceptible tremor: "Why panic! Bring in the emergency report!"
A moment later, a postman who was covered in sweat and disheveled clothes stumbled in, holding a blood-stained letter tightly in his hand. The letter was sealed with wax paint, and the paint had been worn away and was blurred. It was obvious that he had traveled thousands of miles and rushed here. The postman's knees weakened and he fell to the ground. He gasped for air and said in a hoarse voice: "Shi... Your Majesty, urgent report... Xiliang urgent report, General Hu Lin... General Hu Lin sent someone to say... that the Xiongnu invaded in large numbers and mobilized 100,000 pieces of iron." Riding, besiege Yanmen Pass. Now Yanmen Pass has been besieged for five days and five nights. Food and grass have been cut off, water sources have dried up, and the soldiers have suffered heavy casualties. General Hu Lin... General Hu Lin has been hit by several arrows. He is in danger. I beg the prince... I beg the prince to quickly bring reinforcements and rush to Xiliang! "
Xiao Yan stepped forward and grabbed the blood-stained letter. His fingertips turned slightly white from the exertion, and his breathing became rapid. With trembling hands, he tore open the seal of the letter. The paper was soaked with sweat and blood. The handwriting on it was scrawled and messy, with some dark red blood stains. It was obviously written by General Hu Lin himself when he was seriously injured.
"Brother Xiao Yan: The Xiongnu invaded in a large scale, with hundreds of thousands of cavalry pressing down on the territory, and Yanmen Pass is in danger. Now our army's food and grass are cut off, the water sources are exhausted, and more than half of our soldiers have been killed or injured. I have been hit by several arrows, and I may not be able to hold on. The land of Xiliang is a barrier for our family and country, and we must not lose it; the danger of Yanmen Pass is the gateway to Western Xinjiang, and we must guard it. My brother has always been talented and strategic. The brave champion of the three armies, Xiliang is in danger now, the people are in danger, the soldiers are in danger, I implore my brother to return quickly, gather the old troops, and rush to the aid of Yanmen Pass to protect the people of Xiliang and guard the territory of our country. Remember, Xiliang cannot be lost, and Yanmen Pass cannot be broken. Even if we spend the last drop of our blood, we must defend this land of Western Frontier..."
Just over a hundred words, Xiao Yan read it over and over againEvery word, like a sharp knife, pierced into the bottom of his heart. Every blood stain told the crisis and hardship of Xiliang. General Hu Lin, the man who treated him like a brother, taught him how to use soldiers, and protected him, was now in danger with several arrows in his body; the soldiers who fought alongside him were now trapped in a tight siege and suffered heavy casualties; the land he once protected with his life was now being trampled by the Huns' cavalry, and the people were displaced and their lives were in ruins.
"Pfft--" A mouthful of blood spilled from the corner of Xiao Yan's mouth, staining the letter paper in his hand red, as well as his moon-white brocade robe. He only felt a sharp pain in his chest, as if thousands of needles were piercing his heart. His eyesight turned black, but he still held on to the blood-stained letter and refused to let go. Three years of forbearance and stability, three years of waiting and expectation, all came to nothing at this moment, replaced by endless sorrow and anxiety, and responsibility and responsibility engraved in the bone marrow.
"Your Majesty! Your Majesty, how are you?" Uncle Fu heard the noise and hurriedly ran in. When he saw the blood on the corner of Xiao Yan's mouth and the blood-stained letter in his hand, he turned pale with fright and hurriedly stepped forward to help him.
Xiao Yan waved his hand, pushed Uncle Fu's hand away, supported his body, and slowly stood up straight. The grief in his eyes was gradually replaced by determination. It was a determination that was desperate to risk death, and a determination that would leave me alone without any hesitation. He raised his hand to wipe the blood from the corner of his mouth, and his voice was low and powerful, with unquestionable majesty: "Uncle Fu, prepare your armor! Prepare your horse! Get my Hanfeng Sword!"
"Your Majesty, please think again!" Uncle Fu quickly dissuaded, with tears welling up in his eyes, "You were seriously injured three years ago, and your body has not fully recovered yet. Moreover, you have taken off your armor and returned home to live leisurely. The court may not agree with you rushing to Xiliang's aid! Besides, the Xiongnu's 100,000 cavalry are coming with menacing force. Yanmen Pass has been besieged for many days. Rushing to help now is tantamount to pulling teeth from a tiger's mouth and a narrow escape!"
"Think twice?" Xiao Yan sneered and looked to the west, his eyes full of anger and perseverance, "Uncle Fu, do you know that General Hu Lin treats me like a brother, and those Xiliang soldiers are all my brothers and sisters. The land of Xiliang is the land I once protected with my life! Now, they are trapped in a tight siege, their lives hang on a thread, and the people are displaced and suffering. How can I just sit back and do nothing? How can I think twice before taking action?"
He paused and his voice became heavier: "Three years ago, the reason why I returned home was to guard the stability of Chang'an for the soldiers who died in the battle, and to recharge my batteries. When Xiliang needed it in the future, I would put on my armor and rush to the frontier. Now, Xiliang is in trouble, and Yanmen Pass is in emergency. , it’s time for me to go back! Even if I have a near-death experience, even if the court does not support me, even if I am alone, I will never back down! I, Xiao Yan, was born in troubled times and died on the battlefield. It is my destiny to die to protect my country and my brothers and sisters, and I will die without regrets!"
Uncle Fu looked at Xiao Yan's firm gaze and listened to his decisive words. He knew that his persuasion was useless, so he could only nod his head with tears in his eyes: "Old slave...Old slave, go prepare your armor and horses right now!" After saying that, he turned around and ran out in a hurry.
Xiao Yan walked to the desk again, his eyes fell on the topographic map of Xiliang, his fingertips slowly traced the passes and fortresses, and his mind was rapidly thinking about the rescue strategy. The Huns' 100,000 cavalry are approaching fiercely, and Yanmen Pass is now cut off from food and grass. More than half of the soldiers have been killed and wounded, and General Hu Lin has been seriously injured. The situation is already precarious. He is now in Chang'an and has no soldiers in his hands. It is not easy to rush to Xiliang's aid.
He remembered that when he returned home three years ago, a group of old Xiliang tribesmen returned to Chang'an with him because they missed their homeland and were grateful for his kindness. Now they all live in seclusion in the villages outside Chang'an City. These people are all warriors who have experienced hundreds of battles and are brave and good at fighting. If they can be gathered together, they will be a big force. besides,He can also send people to contact other defenders on the border of Xiliang and ask them to send troops for reinforcements. Attacking from both sides may be able to break the siege of Yanmen Pass.
Also, in the court, although he has returned to his hometown to live idle, the Marquis of Jing'an has always been loyal and trusted by the royal family. He may be able to enter the palace to meet the emperor and implore your majesty to send troops to reinforce Xiliang, allocate grain, grass, ordnance, and support Yanmen Pass. However, he also knows that in today's court, treacherous ministers are in power, and His Majesty is addicted to pleasure and has long lost the ambitions of the past. It is not easy to get His Majesty to send troops for reinforcements, and he may even be blocked and excluded by treacherous ministers.
But even so, he would never give up. In order to protect General Lin, for those Xiliang soldiers, for the people of Xiliang, and to protect the territory of his country, he is willing to do whatever it takes, even if it means offending traitorous ministers, even if he offends Long Yan, even if he is alone, he will rush to Xiliang to help Yanmen Pass.
After a while, Uncle Fu came in with a few servants carrying a pair of bright silver armor. The armor was worn by Xiao Yan when he was in Xiliang. The armor was made of cold iron and engraved with fine lines. It could defend against swords and was light and flexible. On the chest of the armor, there was also a large Chinese character "Xiao" engraved on it. It had been tempered on the battlefield and still shone brightly. The Hanfeng Sword was also taken out. The sword was unsheathed and the cold light shone coldly, making the entire study feel cold. It was a sword that had drunk the blood of the Huns and was a sword that protected the land of Xiliang.
Xiao Yan took off his moon-white brocade robe and slowly put on the armor with the help of his servant. The armor still fit him well, but the moment he put it on, he seemed to have returned to the Xiliang battlefield three years ago, back to those days of fighting and blood-stained battlefields. The fatigue and alienation on his body were instantly replaced by the military uniform and vigor, and there was a sense of majesty and determination surrounding him. He took the Hanfeng Sword and held it in his hand. The coldness of the sword came through his fingertips, but it made him more awake and strengthened his determination to rush to Xiliang.
"Uncle Fu," Xiao Yan turned around, looked at Uncle Fu, and said in a serious tone, "I rushed to Xiliang today to rescue Yanmen Pass. It's a dangerous journey. I don't know if I can come back safely. I leave the affairs of the house to you. You must take good care of the house. My servants, protect the foundation of Jing'an Hou Mansion. Also, take care of my family members from the old Xiliang tribe. If I fail to come back this time, tell them not to be sad, not to forget the people of Xiliang, and not to forget the responsibility of protecting the country. "
Uncle Fu knelt down on the ground, and finally couldn't help but shed tears. He choked and said, "Don't worry, Your Majesty, I will fulfill my mission. I will take good care of the affairs of the house, protect the foundation of Jing'an Marquis House, and take good care of the family members of the old tribe. I beg the Prince to take care of yourself and come back safely. I, the servants of the house, and the old tribe are all waiting for your return in Chang'an!"
Xiao Yan nodded slightly, with a trace of tears in his eyes, but he resisted falling. He knew that if he went to Xiliang, he would have a narrow escape from death. Perhaps, he would never come back, never see Uncle Fu again, never see those old Xiliang tribes again, never see the prosperity and stability of Chang'an again. But he had no choice. He was Xiao Yan, the eldest son of the Marquis of Jing'an, and the guardian of Xiliang. It was his innate responsibility to protect his family, his brothers, and his people, even if it cost his life.
"Get up." Xiao Yan said softly, reaching out to help Uncle Fu, "Time is running out and I can't delay any longer. I will set off immediately to gather my old troops and rush to Xiliang."
After saying that, he held the Hanfeng Sword, turned around and walked out of the study, strode across the courtyard and towards the door of the mansion. The leaves of the old locust trees in the courtyard swayed gently in the wind, as if they were seeing him off, but also seemed to be worried about him. The sun shines through the gaps in the leaves and shines on his armor, refracting dazzling light, illuminating his firm figure and his rush to Xiliang., the determination to regard death as home.
Outside the gate of the house, a black and extraordinary horse has been prepared. It was his mount when he was in Xiliang, named "Taxue". It can travel thousands of miles by day and eight hundred at night. It accompanied him in the north and south and made great achievements in battle. When Taxue saw Xiao Yan, she let out a long neigh, as if she was expressing her longing for him, and as if she was getting ready to go to the battlefield with him at any time.
